name: How often does natural stone tile need to be sealed?

mainEntity.name: How often does natural stone tile need to be sealed?

acceptedAnswer.text: Sealing frequency depends on the type of stone, its location, and the amount of daily moisture exposure. In high-use, wet environments like walk-in showers or kitchen backsplashes, porous stones such as marble, travertine, and limestone generally require resealing every 6 to 12 months. Denser stones like granite or certain slates may only need sealing every 1 to 2 years. A straightforward way to test your stone is the water drop test: place a few drops of water on the surface; if the water beads up, the seal is intact, but if it darkens the stone and absorbs, it is time for a fresh coat of penetrating sealer.
acceptedAnswer.description: Most natural stone tiles in wet areas need resealing every 6 to 12 months, while denser stones in dry areas can go 1 to 2 years between treatments.
